title: Prepending a successful bit read
statement: Let $x$ be a finite bit string, let $B$ be a natural number, let $l,l_1,l_0$ be program labels, let $st$ be a seven-register state, let $c$ be an abstract configuration, and let $b$ be a Boolean. Suppose the instruction at $l$ calls the first oracle in whole-input mode with the input-pointer register as its sole argument, every register of $st$ is at most $B$, and the bit of $x$ at position $st.P$ (taken to be false beyond the end of $x$) equals $b$. If there is a bounded, precondition-preserving run from label $l_1$ when $b$ is true, or from label $l_0$ when $b$ is false, with registers initialized from $st$, to $c$, then there is such a run from label $l$ with those same initial registers to $c$.
